description.value: The study investigated face perception, face memory and object memory in semantic dementia and behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia using neuropsychological tasks and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: In this study we used novel experimental tasks, in combination with voxel-based morphometry, to investigate face perception, face memory and object memory in individuals with SD and bvFTD.

description.value: A cross-sectional observational study compared semantic dementia patients, behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia patients and healthy controls.

definition.value: Identity-Matching performance was associated with grey matter intensity in semantic dementia and controls.

spans.text: Total scores on either the Identity-Matching task, the CFMT or the CCMT were entered as covariates into separate design matrices and a positive [1] correlation analysis was performed ( ).
Total scores on either the Identity-Matching task, the CFMT or the CCMT were entered as covariates into separate design matrices and a positive [1] correlation analysis was performed ( ).

value: In the SD group, Identity-Matching performance was predominantly associated with integrity of the right temporal lobe, including the anterior fusiform cortex, inferior temporal gyrus, amygdala and temporal pole. Performance was also associated with integrity of the left temporal pole, left inferior temporal gyrus and left parahippocampal gyrus.

name.value: Semantic dementia + controls: CFMT (Face Memory) – Total score

definition.value: CFMT performance and grey matter intensity were correlated in semantic dementia and controls.

spans.text: Total scores on either the Identity-Matching task, the CFMT or the CCMT were entered as covariates into separate design matrices and a positive [1] correlation analysis was performed ( ).
Total scores on either the Identity-Matching task, the CFMT or the CCMT were entered as covariates into separate design matrices and a positive [1] correlation analysis was performed ( ).

value: Neural correlates of face memory performance in the SD group tended to be left lateralised and were associated with integrity of the left fusiform cortex and temporal pole as well as the anterior portion of the left middle temporal gyrus. In addition, a cluster was identified in the right temporal lobe encompassing the anterior middle temporal gyrus, extending into the right temporal pole and right orbitofrontal cortex.

value: No regions significantly correlated with object memory in SD.

value: In bvFTD, Identity-Matching performance was associated with integrity of the left orbitofrontal cortex extending into the left temporal pole and with the left fusiform gyrus.

value: In bvFTD, memory for faces was associated with integrity of the left temporal pole extending into the left orbitofrontal cortex, with a second region identified in the left insula.

Total scores on either the Identity-Matching task, the CFMT or the CCMT were entered as covariates into separate design matrices and a positive [1] correlation analysis was performed ( ).

value: Object memory in bvFTD was associated with a distinct set of brain regions, including the right frontal opercular cortex extending into the insula, together with the left thalamus.

spans.text: Face-Perception task

description.value: Participants judged whether 40 pairs of neutral-expression faces were identical or different.

stimuli.value: Greyscale faces from the NimStim stimulus set, cropped to remove non-facial features.

instructions.value: Participants were verbally asked whether the two images were the same picture and responded verbally yes or no.

spans.text: Identity-Matching task

description.value: Participants judged whether simultaneously presented face pairs with different emotional expressions depicted the same person across 42 trials.

stimuli.value: Greyscale faces from the NimStim stimulus set, cropped to remove non-facial features.

instructions.value: Participants were verbally asked whether the two pictures were of the same person and responded verbally yes or no.

spans.text: Cambridge Face Memory Test

description.value: Participants learned six faces and identified target faces among two similar distractors across same-image, novel-image, and novel-image-plus-noise sections.

stimuli.value: Six greyscale target faces with hair and other identifying facial features removed.

spans.text: Cambridge Car Memory Test

description.value: Participants learned six target cars and identified target cars among distractors across same-image, novel-image, and novel-image-plus-noise sections.
